writing.prompt: Mahalle pazarı hafta içi müşteri sayısını artırdı. Aynı hafta yağmur durdu ve çarşamba ücretsiz otopark başladı. Satıcı seslerinde biri otoparkı, biri havayı öne çıkarıyor. İki çıkarımı ayıran bir karar notu yaz.
writing.sample: While weekday visits rose, the available count cannot tell us what caused the increase. One stallholder attributes it to free Wednesday parking, whereas another points to the better weather. Neither observation establishes how many visitors came for each reason. I would keep the parking offer for another month and compare Wednesdays with similar days when parking is charged. Record rainfall on all days and ask a small sample what influenced their visit. Parking receipts are necessary to check usage, but they would not be sufficient to rule out the effect of weather. Report the two results separately.
writing.revision: Önerdiğin ölçü iki olası açıklamayı ayırmalı. Kaynaklara duymadıkları bir iddia yükleme.
criteria: İki yorum kaynaklarıyla ve sınırlarıyla verilir.
Öneri ayrım yapmaya çalışan ölçülebilir karşılaştırma sunar.

input.text:
A secondary school kept phones in lockers during the first lesson for four weeks. Its attendance log shows that late arrivals fell in that period. The same week the trial began, a bus company started an earlier route from the largest housing estate. The school newsletter credits the phone rule with the whole improvement.

Two form tutors report that pupils now settle down more quietly. Their notes describe behaviour once pupils are inside, rather than when pupils reach the gate. The pupil council asked for a separate count of children who walk to school. The head intends to retain the phone rule during a further trial, but wants to learn which change affected arrival times.

The log covers the same number of school days before and during the trial, but it does not show how pupils arrived. A second school on the bus route did not introduce the phone rule. Its head has offered to share anonymised arrival records. The pupil council supports the comparison as long as the final report distinguishes those records from the tutors’ descriptions of classroom behaviour.
reading: Kuralın gelişmenin tamamını sağladığını söylemeyi ne zorlaştırıyor?
Aynı dönemde daha erken otobüs seferi başladı
Otobüs de varış zamanını değiştirmiş olabilir.
a bus company started an earlier route
input.transcript:
— The newsletter gives the lockers all the credit. I can say the room is calmer once everyone is sitting down, but that does not explain who gets to school on time.
— I take the new bus. It reaches the gate ten minutes earlier. My friends who walk have the same route as before.
— Then let’s record travel mode and arrival time separately for two more weeks. We need both records before we can compare the groups. The quieter rooms are a separate result.

main: Ulaşım biçimi, varış ve sınıf içi davranış
Kayıtlar varışı ölçer, sınıf sessizliği ayrı bir sonuçtur.
The quieter rooms are a separate result.
detail: Öğrencinin otobüsü ne kadar erken geliyor?

writing.sample: At the tenants’ meeting, the treasurer began describing a repair estimate when a resident asked about next year’s rent. The chair replied that the rent question mattered, but asked the resident to hold it until the scope of the estimate was clear. The treasurer explained that the quote covered the roof above two stairwells, not the entire building. Another tenant asked whether the lower stairwell had been inspected. The chair recorded that as an outstanding question and invited the treasurer to respond before returning to rent. The meeting agreed to request a second inspection and discuss the budget after receiving it.
writing.revision: Bir soruyu karar gibi yazma. Sonraki iki adımın sırasını denetle.
criteria: Açık kalan soru ile alınan karar ayrı.

input.text:
The review panel met to decide whether evening library hours should continue. Its chair, Mara, asked each member to name one result that could change their recommendation. Dr Ellis said the exit survey showed that late visitors valued the extra hour. He added that the survey included only people who stayed until closing. Before he could explain the limitation, another member, Priya, began asking about staffing costs. Mara intervened gently: “We still have Dr Ellis’s unanswered point about who was represented.” She asked Priya to hold her question, then invited Ellis to finish. He said the results supported keeping the trial for registered users, but did not establish that access improved for people who left early. The panel agreed to check both groups before a permanent decision.

In the draft minutes, the secretary had combined Ellis’s observation and Priya’s question under “Reasons to keep the trial”. Mara returned the draft with two notes. The survey established a preference among the respondents; it did not establish what happened to other visitors. Staffing costs were raised as a question and were not yet known. Priya checked the revised wording and asked that the cost comparison be the first item at the next meeting, once the two visitor groups had been identified.
reading: Başkan hangi soruyu önce bitirmek istiyor?
Başkan örneklem noktasına dönüp personel sorusunu sıraya koyuyor.
input.transcript:
— Before we move on, I want to return to the question we have not answered. Dr Ellis, you said the survey reflected visitors who stayed until closing.
— Yes. We did not ask people who left earlier, so I can’t say whether the later hour helped them.
— I was going to ask about staffing, but I see that my question came before that point was finished.
— Thank you. Let’s record both questions separately. First, who benefited? Then, what would the additional hour cost?
input.preparation: Sıra: Mara → Ellis → Priya → Mara. Soruların sahiplerini, gündem sırasını ve açık kalan bilgiyi not et.

detail: We did not ask people who left earlier

concepts.label: Tutumun sahibini sınama
concepts.correct: ‘Of course.’ may carry the character’s impatience in the context.
concepts.explanation: Karakterin bakışına yeni geçilmişse kısa değerlendirme doğrudan anlatıcı hükmü olarak okunmayabilir.
guided: ‘She checked the key. Brilliant. It didn’t fit.’ Brilliant tutumu: irony / praise
‘He shut the window. Surely they had heard him.’ Varsayımın sahibi: character / quoted witness
transfer: ‘Eva counted her coins. More than enough, obviously. Then she noticed the price.’ İlk yargı: confidence / certainty of the new price
‘Mara looked at the empty shelf. How kind of them to leave the labels.’ Kind hangi işlevde? irony / neutral description
delayed: ‘Leo checked the clock. They must have left already.’ Muhtemel dayanak: Leo’s inference / confirmed departure
‘Ada read the draft. A mistake, perhaps, although she could not name it.’ Tutum: uncertainty / verified error

concepts.label: Karakterin zamansal bakışı
concepts.incorrect: In third person, tomorrow must always become the next day.
concepts.correct: Tomorrow can keep the character’s immediate temporal viewpoint.
concepts.explanation: Anlatıcı mesafesini artırınca the next day, yakın karakter bakışında tomorrow kullanılabilir.
guided: ‘He would go tomorrow. No more waiting.’ Yakın bakışın zaman sözcüğü: ___
“Today of all days!” düşüncesini yakın biçimde tut: ___ of all days!
transfer: ‘The next morning she left.’ Mesafeli eşdeğer: the following morning / this morning
‘There was no time now.’ Karaktere yakın sözcük: ___
delayed: ‘Could they really be here already?’ Karakterin mekânı: ___
‘He wondered if she had arrived the previous evening.’ Mesafeli zaman ifadesi: the previous evening / tonight

writing.prompt: Bir galeri eski bir haritayı depoda tutacak. Tomas önce kararı mantıklı buluyor, sonra bir kopya yapılabileceğini hatırlıyor fakat küratörün sözünden emin değil. Önce bakışına yakın anlat, sonra son iki olguyu tarafsız not olarak ver.
writing.sample: When the gallery announced that the old map would remain in storage, Tomas read the notice twice. Sensible, he supposed. The paper was fragile and the room was too bright. Still, a careful copy could have been displayed. The curator had said as much last month, hadn’t she? Tomas could not remember the exact words. Perhaps he had heard what he wanted to hear. At the meeting, he asked whether the archive might show a facsimile instead. The curator welcomed the suggestion but explained that the copy had not yet been checked for colour accuracy. Meeting record: the colour check is pending, with no final display decision.
writing.revision: Yargının kime ait olduğunu iki sürümde karşılaştır. Düşünceyi kurul kararı gibi yazma.
criteria: Yakın bakış sözcük ve zaman seçimiyle tanınabilir.
Tarafsız sürüm yalnız doğrulanmış olguları taşır.

input.text:
Nora returned to the station just as her bus pulled away. Of course. The timetable had said ten past, unless the town had quietly moved the clock again. She checked her phone: 22:08. The driver had stopped at the exit gate to let a van pass. “Could you wait?” she called, though she knew what he would say. He looked at the empty road, then at the queue behind her. It was not his fault, naturally. Nobody had told him that the connection from the clinic was late. Nora stepped back. The next bus was in forty minutes. Plenty of time to explain to her sister why she had missed dinner, and why the soup would be cold. She opened a message, deleted it, and began again.

From the bench she could see a notice by the gate. The driver had waited for an ambulance at the previous stop. So that was what the dispatcher had been trying to tell her at the clinic. Or had he? She could remember only the woman’s finger pointing toward the exit. Weeks later her sister recalled the evening differently: she had offered to collect Nora, and the text on her phone said there was no rush. Nora’s unfinished reply, still saved in the drafts folder, began with an apology for keeping everyone waiting.
reading: Of course, saat iması ve Plenty of time birlikte neyi gösteriyor?
Nora’nın sabırsız ve alaycı bakışı olgusal anlatıdan duyuluyor
Bu değerlendirmeleri doğrulanmış olay gibi okumak, bakış değişimini kaçırır.
unless the town had quietly moved the clock again
input.transcript:
— The narrator first gives the missed bus as an event. Then “Of course” moves close to Nora’s impatient thought.
— So that phrase belongs to the narrator’s verdict?
— I wouldn’t say verdict. The timetable and the clock are coloured by Nora’s suspicion.
— Would “naturally” be another example?
— Yes. It may carry her self-correction. The narration stays in the third person while briefly taking on her language. We can read the shading without treating it as a direct quotation.
input.preparation: Sıra: okur → editör → okur → moderatör → okur. Kesin olay ile olası tutum arasındaki farkı incele.

Anlatıcı tüm sahneyi birinci kişide anlatıyor
Son cümle alıntı ile bakışa yaklaşma arasında sınır çizer.
